prompt.context_jp: 一人静かに仕事に集中する時間こそ___、彼にとっての休日の過ごし方だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一人静かに仕事に集中する時間こそ___、彼にとっての休日の過ごし方だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after こそ to identify this as 'precisely the way he spends his days off'?

feedback.correct_en: こそ pairs with が here to exhaustively identify THIS (and nothing else) as his way of enjoying a day off. It singles out the subject as the one definitive answer.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would weaken the emphatic 'precisely this' feeling that こそ sets up. を doesn't fit since 時間 is the subject of だった, not an object.

contrast_examples.en: This is the real thing (and nothing else).

prompt.context_jp: 若い看護師たちの夏休み計画の輪の中で――
prompt.prompt_jp: 医師の夏美___、その輪に自然に交ざりながらも、どこか浮かない表情でいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces Natsumi as the topic being described?

feedback.correct_en: Natsumi has already been set up as a known figure; は presents her as the topic and the sentence then describes her state. This is classic topic-は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark her as newly identified/new information, but she's already contextually known and the sentence is describing her, not identifying who.

contrast_examples.en: It was Natsumi who was troubled. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 南の島の話題に――
prompt.prompt_jp: 南の島の話題に、彼女の心___動かなかったわけではない。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for 'her heart' as the subject that did (not) move?

feedback.correct_en: Inside the 〜わけではない clause, 心 is the subject of 動かなかった; が marks it neutrally as the thing that moved/didn't move.
feedback.incorrect_en: は here would awkwardly topicalize 心 inside a subordinate clause and shift focus; が is the natural subject marker in this embedded negation pattern.

contrast_examples.jp: 気持ちが動かなかったわけではない。
contrast_examples.en: It's not that my feelings didn't stir.

contrast_examples.jp: 気持ちは動かなかった。
contrast_examples.en: My feelings (as for them) didn't stir.

prompt.context_jp: 休みらしい休みを取らずに働き続けてきた身には――
prompt.prompt_jp: その明るさ___少しまぶしい。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for 'that brightness' as the thing causing the feeling?

feedback.correct_en: With sensation adjectives like まぶしい, the stimulus is typically marked with が — it's the thing that IS dazzling (new/identifying information).
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 明るさ a contrastive topic, suggesting 'as for that brightness (versus other things)…', which doesn't fit this descriptive moment.

contrast_examples.jp: 日差しはまぶしいが、風は涼しい。
contrast_examples.en: The sunlight is dazzling, but the wind is cool. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: そんな会話に、
prompt.prompt_jp: 内線の呼び出し音___割って入った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle introduces the interrupting phone ring?

feedback.correct_en: The ringing phone is new information bursting into the scene — classic が for a newly appearing event/subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would wrongly treat the phone ring as an established topic. を doesn't work since 割って入る is intransitive here.

contrast_examples.en: The phone (as for it) didn't ring.

prompt.context_jp: 若い看護師が夏美に質問する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 先生___休みの日って 何してるんですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle sets 'Sensei' as the topic of the question?

feedback.correct_en: The nurse is asking ABOUT Natsumi — 'as for you, Sensei, what do you do?' This is pure topic-は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly identify (as if answering 'who does what on days off'). に would mean 'to Sensei', not fitting here.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生は何してるんですか？
先生が何かしましたか？

prompt.context_jp: 人混みの中にいると――
prompt.prompt_jp: 人の密度で暑いの___ますます暑くなるし
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (Kuwano is describing how heat intensifies.)

feedback.correct_en: '暑いの' (the already-hot thing) is the subject of a descriptive change; が presents it as the thing undergoing the change in this neutral description.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a contrastive topic ('as for the heat…'), which breaks the flow of Kuwano's running complaint.

contrast_examples.jp: 暑いのがもっと暑くなる。

contrast_examples.en: The heat (as for it) I can bear.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野「いや」
prompt.prompt_jp: 1人のほう___足手まといがいなくていいしな
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for 'being alone (compared to with others)'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜ほうが is the fixed comparative pattern meaning 'the X option is better.' が is required to pick out 'being alone' as the preferred alternative.
feedback.incorrect_en: は doesn't work in the comparative 〜ほうがいい pattern; swapping to は breaks the comparison structure.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野の天気予報。
prompt.prompt_jp: 気温___うなぎ登りだ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for 'as for the temperature'?

feedback.correct_en: Kuwano is commenting about what the temperature will do — topicalizing 気温 and predicating 'it'll skyrocket.' Topic-は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would identify ('it's the temperature that…'), which doesn't match a general weather report tone.

contrast_examples.en: The temperature rose! (observation of new fact)

prompt.context_jp: 母・育代の言葉。
prompt.prompt_jp: 家族の笑顔___見られるってことは もう何ものにも 変えがたい幸せなのよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (potential verb 見られる)

feedback.correct_en: With potential 見られる ('being able to see'), the thing seen is normally marked with が — 'being able to see family smiles' is itself the subject of the nominalized phrase.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is possible with some potentials but less natural with 見られる here; は would topicalize and break the 〜ってこと nominalization.

contrast_examples.en: As for Mt. Fuji, you can't see it.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野「日曜まで病院にいたんじゃ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 気___晴れるときがないですね
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for '(one's) spirits lifting'?

feedback.correct_en: 気が晴れる is a fixed expression — 'one's mood clears up' — and takes が as the subject marker.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気を晴らす (transitive, 'to lift one's spirits') exists, but 晴れる is intransitive so を is wrong. は would contrast, breaking the idiom.

prompt.context_jp: 千鶴の彼氏論。
prompt.prompt_jp: 休みの日を どう楽しませてくれるか___彼氏の大事なポイントよね
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (embedded question + predicate)

feedback.correct_en: An embedded question 〜か ('HOW he'll entertain you') functions as the subject being defined as 大事なポイント. が links the defining subject to its identification.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a topic ('as for how he entertains you…'), which is less natural when you are DEFINING what the key point is.

contrast_examples.en: What you say is the issue.
As for what to say, it's up to you.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野がバスの席の謎を解説。
prompt.prompt_jp: 1人で乗ってんの___俺たち2人だけなんだ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits? (identifying who the solo riders are)

feedback.correct_en: This is exhaustive-listing が: 'the ones riding alone are ONLY us two.' が picks out the uniquely identified subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would read as a topic ('as for riding alone, it's only us'), losing the 'and no one else' exhaustive flavor.

contrast_examples.en: The only one who came was him.
The one who came was him. (also identifying, but less exclusive)

prompt.context_jp: 桑野「僕はね 自己啓発の一環で乗ったんですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: あなた___単に ひとり寂しく乗ったんでしょう？
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the contrast with 僕?

feedback.correct_en: Kuwano is contrasting himself (僕は) with Natsumi (あなたは) — classic contrastive-は. 'I did X, but YOU just did Y.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make it sound like identifying the subject neutrally, losing the 'you, unlike me' contrast that's the whole point of his jab.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野、花火の話を切り出す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 見えるんです ウチの事務所のビルの屋上___ 花火です
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'from the rooftop'?

feedback.correct_en: から marks the point FROM WHICH the fireworks can be seen — a source/vantage point.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the location of an action, but 見える is a spontaneous-perception verb; 'from (vantage)' is から. が would mark the subject, not a location.

contrast_examples.jp: 屋上から富士山が見える。
contrast_examples.en: You can see Mt. Fuji from the rooftop.
To do fireworks on the rooftop.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野の花火講釈。
prompt.prompt_jp: 銀色のほう___温度が高いから その分 作るのが難しいんだよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for 'the silver one (compared to others)'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜ほうが高い is the comparative pattern: 'the silver one has a higher temperature (than the other).' Comparative ほう takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は breaks the explicit comparison; you'd lose the 'silver vs. gold' comparative meaning.

contrast_examples.en: This one is expensive. (topic, no comparison stated)

prompt.context_jp: 摩耶が桑野の遠回しな言い方を翻訳して言う。
prompt.prompt_jp: 休みを___あげようという この人なりの思いやりよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb form fits — 'to let (you) take a break'?

feedback.correct_en: 取らせてあげる is the causative-benefactive: 'to let someone take (a break) for their benefit.' That matches Maya's point — Kuwano is giving Eiji permission.
feedback.incorrect_en: 取って would mean Kuwano takes a break himself. 取られて is passive, 'having it taken', which doesn't fit.

prompt.context_jp: みちるが英治をからかう。
prompt.prompt_jp: 沙織ちゃんと結婚したら ___に敷かれるの見えてるね
prompt.prompt_en: Fill the blank in the idiom meaning 'to be under her thumb'.

feedback.correct_en: 尻に敷かれる is a fixed idiom: literally 'to be sat on' — meaning to be henpecked / under the wife's control.
feedback.incorrect_en: 背中 or 手 don't form the idiom. Only 尻に敷かれる conveys the henpecked-husband image.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は奥さんの尻に敷かれている。

prompt.context_jp: 夏美が薬を処方する。
prompt.prompt_jp: お薬 ___おきますから
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits a doctor prescribing medicine?

feedback.correct_en: 薬を出す is the standard collocation for a doctor 'prescribing/issuing' medicine.
feedback.incorrect_en: 作る (make) is for pharmacists compounding; 売る (sell) sounds commercial/odd for a doctor.

contrast_examples.jp: 胃薬を出しておきますね。
contrast_examples.en: I'll prescribe you some stomach medicine.

prompt.context_jp: 摩耶が桑野に休日の過ごし方を説く。
prompt.prompt_jp: いい仕事をするためには 外に___ことも必要よ
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb phrase fits — 'going out (into the world)'?

feedback.correct_en: 外に出ていく — 'to go out' — is the natural phrase. Maya is telling him to leave the office and engage with the world.
feedback.incorrect_en: 入っていく (go in) and 降りていく (go down) don't fit the 'get out there' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: The courage to go out into the world.

prompt.context_jp: はとバスの窓口係員の応対。
prompt.prompt_jp: はい ___くださいませ
prompt.prompt_en: Which polite expression fits — 'please wait a moment'?

feedback.correct_en: 少々お待ちくださいませ is the set polite service-industry phrase — maximally polite with お〜ください + ませ.
feedback.incorrect_en: ちょっと待って is casual; 少し待つ lacks any polite form and isn't a command.

contrast_examples.jp: 少々お待ちくださいませ。

prompt.context_jp: 桑野が夏美の買い物をからかう。
prompt.prompt_jp: こういうとこ来ると― ___で 余計な物 買っちゃうタイプですか？
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits — 'on a whim / impulsively'?

feedback.correct_en: 気まぐれ means 'whim / fickleness' — exactly fits 'the type who impulsively buys unnecessary stuff.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 気楽 means 'carefree' and 気の毒 means 'pitiable' — neither fits the 'impulse-buy' nuance.

contrast_examples.en: I bought it on a whim.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野の揺れる心境を描写する地の文。
prompt.prompt_jp: 独りでいたいだけなのに、その独りがだんだん___にくくなってきた
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits — 'hard to handle/manage'?

feedback.correct_en: 取り扱いにくい means 'hard to handle/manage.' The 'solitude' is becoming unwieldy — that's the sense.
feedback.incorrect_en: 取り替え (replace) and 取り下げ (withdraw) don't convey 'hard to manage.'

contrast_examples.jp: この問題は取り扱いにくい。
contrast_examples.en: This issue is hard to handle.

prompt.context_jp: 夏美に先約があると知って。
prompt.prompt_jp: ___越されたのが悔しかったのか、桑野の口調に棘が戻ってきた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes 'to be beaten to it / outpaced'?

feedback.correct_en: 先を越される is a fixed idiom: 'to be beaten to the punch / outpaced.' Kuwano was going to invite her, but Michiru got there first.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手を越す / 口を越す are not set phrases with this meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: ライバルに先を越された。
contrast_examples.en: My rival beat me to it.

prompt.context_jp: 看護師が夏美を叱る。
prompt.prompt_jp: ダメですよ 休みは ちゃんと___
prompt.prompt_en: Which ending fits — '(you) have to take breaks'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜ないと (short for 〜ないといけない) means 'you have to.' It's the natural 'you need to take breaks properly' meaning.
feedback.incorrect_en: 取れないし ('can't take and…') contradicts the message. 取らなくて is just the te-form of negation, not an obligation.

prompt.context_jp: 夏の朝、桑野が一人事務所で図面に向かう場面の描写として、より自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which sentence sounds more natural as scene-setting narration?

choices.text: 夏の朝、桑野は誰もいない事務所で図面に向かい合っていた。
夏の朝、桑野が誰もいない事務所は図面に向かい合っていた。

feedback.correct_en: 桑野は marks him as the topic being described; 事務所で marks the location. This is the natural reading.
feedback.incorrect_en: B swaps particles incoherently — 桑野が as subject is okay in isolation, but 事務所は with で missing makes it ungrammatical here.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は部屋で本を読んでいた。
contrast_examples.en: He was reading a book in the room.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が部屋は本を読んでいた。

prompt.context_jp: 入院患者が担当医の夏美に土日の勤務を確認する場面。より自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural from a patient to her doctor?

choices.text: 先生 今度の土日も いてくださるんでしょう？
先生 今度の土日も いてあげるんでしょう？

feedback.correct_en: 〜てくださる is the honorific benefactive — 'you (kindly) will be here for me.' Patient to doctor is a classic context.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜てあげる is used when the SPEAKER does a favor for the listener. A patient saying the doctor 'あげる' for herself is nonsensical.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生が助けてくださった。

prompt.context_jp: みちるが英治に発破をかける。より自然な口語は？
prompt.prompt_en: Which casual challenge sounds more natural?

choices.text: “休みの日を どう使おうと 俺の自由だ”くらい言ってみたら？
“休みの日を どう使うので 俺の自由だ”くらい言ってみたら？

feedback.correct_en: 〜(よ)うと is 'no matter how I use…' — the natural concessive pattern meaning 'whatever I do with my day off, it's my freedom.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜ので is a reason connector ('because'), which makes no sense here — 'because I use my day off, it's my freedom' is incoherent.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が何と言おうと、私はやる。
contrast_examples.en: No matter what anyone says, I'll do it.

prompt.context_jp: 夏美の自戒。より自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which version is more natural?

choices.text: “時間があれば”なんて言ってると、結局 一緒に行く相手がいないのよね
“時間があれば”なんて言うと、結局 一緒に行く相手をいないのよね

feedback.correct_en: 〜ていると expresses a habitual state ('if I keep saying…'), and 相手がいない uses が for the existence verb いる. Both are standard.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 相手を いない is ungrammatical — いる takes が, not を. 〜と alone is also less natural than 〜ていると for 'keep doing' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 一緒に行く相手がいない。
contrast_examples.en: I have no one to go with.

prompt.context_jp: 桑野がビルの屋上の特等席を自慢する。より自然なのは？
prompt.prompt_en: Which version is more natural?

choices.text: このことはね 誰も知らないんです
このことがね 誰は知らないんです

feedback.correct_en: このことは topicalizes 'this' as what's being discussed; 誰も with a negative verb means 'nobody.' Natural flow.
feedback.incorrect_en: 誰は is ungrammatical — 誰 ('who') cannot be topicalized with は in a plain negative statement; 誰も is the right indefinite + negation pattern.
